Science of the Room

Module 5 — Music Psychology & Sonic Design

Design functional score arcs using arousal valence mapping, ISO sequencing, and channel control.

Music is your co instructor. Sound design shapes effort, emotion, and meaning.

Why this module exists

Track selection by taste alone produces inconsistent outcomes. Sonic design requires explicit intent: what state you are initiating, amplifying, and integrating.

Core concepts

Arousal valence map

Classify tracks by energy and emotional tone.

ISO principle

ISO means matching the present state first, then shifting gradually toward the target state.

Five Channel Score

  1. Percussion
  2. Harmony
  3. Texture
  4. Vocals
  5. Silence

BPM ranges by arc phase

| Phase | BPM range | Primary function | |—|—:|—| | Arrival | 70 to 95 | Ground and orient | | Warm build | 95 to 115 | Mobilize and commit | | Escalation | 115 to 132 | Increase intensity | | Cathartic peak | 130 to 152 | Concentrated output | | Integration | 95 to 118 | Recover coherence | | Landing | 60 to 90 | Downshift and consolidate |

What the evidence actually says

Music can improve affective response and adherence for many participants. Effects depend on preference, context, culture, and task demand.

Practicum

  1. Build one sixty minute score map.
  2. Annotate each track using five channels.
  3. Test alternative peak tracks.
  4. Add planned silence windows.

Deliverable

Submit a Sonic Design Score with arc map, channel annotations, and contingency swaps.
